root_cause.text: The error path in ksmbd_tcp_new_connection() calls free_transport(), which lacks the necessary decrement of the active_num_conn counter, causing it to leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces free_transport(t) with ksmbd_tcp_disconnect(KSMBD_TRANS(t)) in the kthread_run() failure case, because free_transport() does not decrement active_num_conn as stated in the commit message.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add forward declaration of static function ksmbd_tcp_disconnect to fix implicit declaration warning/error when used before its definition.
intent_record.what: Added a forward declaration of the static function `ksmbd_tcp_disconnect` that takes a `struct ksmbd_transport *` parameter, placed after the existing forward declarations.
intent_record.how: This change provides a function prototype to the compiler, ensuring that any calls to `ksmbd_tcp_disconnect` before its actual definition are not treated as implicit declarations, thus preventing potential compilation warnings or errors and enabling proper type checking.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace improper cleanup with proper TCP disconnect on connection thread creation failure to prevent resource leaks.
intent_record.what: In the error path of `ksmbd_tcp_new_connection`, the call to `free_transport(t)` is replaced with `ksmbd_tcp_disconnect(KSMBD_TRANS(t))`.
intent_record.how: When creating a new connection fails (handler is an error pointer), the code now calls `ksmbd_tcp_disconnect` on the transport instead of `free_transport`. This ensures the TCP socket is properly disconnected and cleaned up before any further freeing.
